title: FHFA House Price Index — Quarterly Index with Monthly Tables (2026Q3 and September 2026 data)
source: FHFA: two FHFA primaries fetched direct 2026-09-06 — (1) fhfa.gov/data/hpi (HTTP 200, 89,663 bytes), the agency's own "2026 HPI Release Dates" table, row "Tuesday, November 24 | Quarterly Index (with Monthly Tables) | September 2026 and 2026Q3"; and (2) the published 2026Q2 report (fhfa.gov/document/d/hpi/fhfa-house-price-index-report-2026q2, HTTP 200, 1,522,949 bytes, 41 pages, released 2026-08-25), whose Notes section states FHFA will release "the next quarterly report (including data for the third quarter of 2026 and monthly data for September 2026) on November 24, 2026". Promoted estimate → confirmed by this event's own initial research, on the precedent that the no-self-confirm limit binds the sweep that DISCOVERED an event (new-home-sales-2026-11-25), not its independent second look. No release time is stated on either primary and none is claimed here. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: The calendar's first house-PRICE entry and its only structurally lapse-proof print. FHFA is funded by assessments on Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and the FHLBanks, which 12 U.S.C. 4516(f)(2)-(3) declares "not ... Government or public funds or appropriated money" and exempts from apportionment under chapter 15 of title 31 — the Antideficiency Act machinery that stops an appropriated agency in a funding lapse. The record matches the statute: 222 of 222 months since the monthly series began in March 2008 carry a release, and 68 of 68 releases since 2021-01-01 landed on the last Tuesday of their month, including 2018-12-27 and 2019-01-23 inside the 35-day shutdown and the whole 2025 lapse that pushed Census's September-2025 new-home-sales data to a 105-day lag. Reaches no model and no measurable price: FHFA HPI appears nowhere in the Atlanta Fed's GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx (0 hits across both sheets, re-fetched 2026-09-06), which schedules NO vintage of any kind on 2026-11-24, and no house playbook is macro-keyed (0 hits). Its release slot is 100% confounded: the Conference Board publishes Consumer Confidence at 10:00 ET on the last Tuesday of every month, so all 68 measured release days are also Consumer Confidence days, and the tape claim is unattributable rather than null. Discovered during the new-home-sales-2026-11-25 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06).
